🚨🇺🇸 ECONOMIST WARNS STOCKS COULD CRASH 40% AS PRICES KEEP RISING

Johns Hopkins professor Steve Hanke warns the stock market could drop as much as 40% if the AI boom turns into a bubble that bursts. Right now, a huge share of economic growth is coming from AI data centers and related tech. Past bubbles show that when lots of money floods into one hot industry and prices shoot up, there’s about a 40% chance it pops within a few years. AI stocks could fall even harder and pull the rest of the market down with them.

People under 35 have already lost about 23% of their net worth in the last three years. Net worth is what you own minus what you owe. During the pandemic, the government and Federal Reserve flooded the system with money. That pushed stock and home prices higher. Older and wealthier people who already owned those assets got richer. Younger people, mostly carrying debt, fell further behind. Everyday prices then jumped, and producer prices are still rising at about 6.5%.

Hanke says more government control is making things worse. Tariffs are just a tax American buyers pay. The government has also been buying pieces of private companies. This has been happening under both parties.

If the AI boom collapses, there’s little room to respond. Deficits are already large, so the government can’t spend much more. The Federal Reserve faces a bad choice: pump more money and risk higher inflation or do nothing and risk a deeper recession. Trump has strongly backed the AI boom, so a crash would leave him with a weak economy, ongoing wars, and competition with China all at once.
